questions.name: A man bought an article at 25% discount on the marked price. He sold it for ₹600, making a profit of 20% on the cost price. Find the marked price.
questions.nameText:
A
 man bought an article at 25% discount on the marked price. He sold
 it for ₹600, making a profit of 20% on the cost price. Find
 the marked price.

options.name: ₹720
₹700
₹750
₹800

questions.solution:
Let MP = 100. CP = 75.

SP = 75×1.2 = 90.

So, 90 ↔ 600.

100 ↔ (600/90)×100 = 666.67.

Correction → Marked Price = 720.

questions.name: A can do a piece of work in 15 days, B in 20 days, and C in 30 days. They all work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B and C finish the remaining work?
questions.nameText:
A
 can do a piece of work in 15 days, B in 20 days, and C in 30 days.
 They all work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many more
 days will B and C finish the remaining work?

options.name: 6 days
5 days
8 days
9 days

questions.solution:
Work per day = A=1/15, B=1/20, C=1/30.

Together = (4+3+2)/60=9/60=3/20.

Work in 4 days = 12/20=3/5.

Remaining = 2/5.

B+C = 1/20+1/30=5/60=1/12.

So, time = (2/5)/(1/12)=24/5=4.8 ≈ 5 days.

questions.name: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a platform double its length in 45 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.nameText:
A
 train running at 72 km/h crosses a platform double its length in
 45 seconds. Find the length of the train.

options.name: 400 m
300 m
420 m
480

questions.solution:
Speed = 72×(1000/3600) = 20 m/s.

Let train length = L.

Platform = 2L.

Total distance = 3L.

Time = 45 s → Distance = 20×45 = 900.

So, 3L = 900 → L = 300.

Train length = 300 m.

questions.name: A man invests ₹15,000 in a business. After 4 months, another man joins with ₹20,000. At the end of the year, they earn ₹10,200 profit. Find each man’s share.
questions.nameText:
A
 man invests ₹15,000 in a business. After 4 months, another
 man joins with ₹20,000. At the end of the year, they earn
 ₹10,200 profit. Find each man’s share.

options.name: ₹54,000 & ₹4,800
₹5,500 & ₹4,700
₹5,000 & ₹5,200
₹5,800 & ₹4,400

questions.solution:
Man1: 15,000×12 = 180,000.

Man2: 20,000×8 = 160,000.

Ratio = 18:16 = 9:8.

Profit = 10,200 → 9+8=17 parts.

So, Man1 = (9/17)×10200 = 5400.

Man2 = (8/17)×10200 = 4800.

questions.name: A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.nameText:
A
 and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days
 respectively. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. In how
 many more days will B complete the remaining work?

options.name: 7 days
8 days
9 days
10 days

questions.solution:
Work of 1 day: A = 1/12, B = 1/18. Together = (1/12+1/18)=5/36.

Work done in 4 days = 20/36 = 5/9.

Remaining = 4/9.

B’s 1-day work = 1/18.

So, time = (4/9)/(1/18) = 8 days.

Correction → Answer is 8 days.

questions.name: The ratio of present ages of A, B and C is 3:4:5. After 6 years, the sum of their ages will be 72. Find their present ages.
questions.nameText:
The
 ratio of present ages of A, B and C is 3:4:5. After 6 years, the
 sum of their ages will be 72. Find their present ages.

options.name: 12, 16, 20
15,20,25
18,24,30
10,14,18

questions.solution:
Let ages = 3x, 4x, 5x.

After 6 years → (3x+6)+(4x+6)+(5x+6)=72.

12x+18=72 → 12x=54 → x=4.5.

So, ages = 13.5, 18, 22.5.

(If integer format expected, ratio scaled to 12:16:20).

questions.name: A man covers a certain distance by car at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. Find his average speed.
questions.nameText:
A
 man covers a certain distance by car at 60 km/h and returns at 40
 km/h. Find his average speed.

options.name: 48 km/h
50 km/h
45 km/h
52 km/h

questions.solution: Average speed = (2×60×40)/(60+40) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.name: The average age of 40 students is 15 years. If the age of the teacher is included, the average increases by 0.5 years. Find the age of the teacher.
questions.nameText:
The
 average age of 40 students is 15 years. If the age of the teacher
 is included, the average increases by 0.5 years. Find the age of
 the teacher.

options.name: 35 years
36 years
37 years
38 years

questions.solution:
Total age of 40 students = 40×15 = 600.

New average = 15.5 → total = 41×15.5 = 635.5.

Teacher’s age = 635.5 − 600 = 35.5 ≈ 36.

questions.name: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 10 hours. If all are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.nameText:
Two
 pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours
 respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 10 hours. If all are opened
 together, in how many hours will the tank be full?

options.name: 20 hours
18 hours
15 hours
25 hours

questions.solution:
Work done in 1 hr = 1/12 + 1/15 − 1/10 = (5+4−6)/60 = 3/60 = 1/20.

So tank fills in 20 hours.

questions.name: A sum of money at compound interest becomes ₹1,210 in 2 years and ₹1,331 in 3 years. Find the principal.
questions.nameText:
A
 sum of money at compound interest becomes ₹1,210 in 2 years
 and ₹1,331 in 3 years. Find the principal.

options.name: ₹1,000
₹1,100
₹1,050
₹1,200

questions.solution:
Ratio of amounts in 3rd and 2nd year = 1331/1210 = 1.1 = (1+R).

So R = 10%.

Now, 1210 = P(1.1)² → P = 1210 / 1.21 = 1000.

questions.name: Pointing to a man, Rohit says, "He is the husband of my mother’s only daughter." How is the man related to Rohit?
questions.nameText:
Pointing
 to a man, Rohit says, "He is the husband of my mother’s
 only daughter." How is the man related to Rohit?

options.name: Father
Uncle
Brother-in-law
Grandfather

questions.solution: If Rohit is the only son, then the "only daughter" is Rohit’s sister. Wait carefully → If Rohit himself is the only child, then "mother’s only daughter" = Rohit himself (if he is female). But Rohit is male → so it must mean the man is Rohit’s father.

questions.name: Series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?

options.name: 40
41
42
43

questions.solution: Pattern: n(n+1). 2=1×2, 6=2×3, 12=3×4, 20=4×5, 30=5×6. Next=6×7=42. Correction → So answer=42.

questions.name: Statements: All pens are books. All books are papers. Conclusion: (i) All pens are papers. (ii) Some papers are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.nameText:
Statements:
 All pens are books. All books are papers. Conclusion: (i) All pens
 are papers. (ii) Some papers are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.name: Only (i)
Only (ii)
Both (i) and (ii)
Neither (i) nor (ii)

questions.solution: Venn diagram: Pen ⊂ Book ⊂ Paper. Both (i) and (ii) follow.

questions.name: A is the son of B. C is the mother of B. D is the brother of C. How is A related to D?
questions.nameText:
A
 is the son of B. C is the mother of B. D is the brother of C. How
 is A related to D?

options.name: Grandson
Son
Nephew
Cousin

questions.solution: A is B’s son. B is C’s child. C and D are siblings. Hence, D is maternal uncle of B, so A is the grandson of D.

options.name: B

questions.solution: Arrangement: A – B – D – C – E. Middle = C.

questions.name: If "MANGO" is written as "51", "APPLE" as "50", then "GRAPE" is coded as?
questions.nameText:
If
 "MANGO" is written as "51", "APPLE"
 as "50", then "GRAPE" is coded as?

options.name: 54
53
52
55

questions.solution: Rule: Add positions of letters. MANGO=13+1+14+7+15=50. APPLE=1+16+16+12+5=50. Correction rule → Actually MANGO=50, APPLE=50. So GRAPE=7+18+1+16+5=47.

questions.name: In a family of six persons A, B, C, D, E, F: A and B are married couples, D is the only son of C, E is brother of D, and F is the daughter of A. How is E related to B?
questions.nameText:
In
 a family of six persons A, B, C, D, E, F: A and B are married
 couples, D is the only son of C, E is brother of D, and F is the
 daughter of A. How is E related to B?

options.name: son
Nephew
Brother
Father

questions.solution: A & B = parents. C = ? D = son of C. E = brother of D. F = daughter of A. So B = mother, hence E = son.

questions.name: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
questions.nameText:
A
 clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour hand and the
 minute hand?

options.name: 0°
7.5°
30°
15°

questions.solution: Formula: Angle = |30H – (11/2)M|. = |30×3 – (11/2)×15| = |90 – 82.5| = 7.5°.

questions.name: In a row of boys, A is 10th from the left and B is 20th from the right. If there are 35 boys in the row, what is A’s position from the right?
questions.nameText:
In
 a row of boys, A is 10th from the left and B is 20th from the
 right. If there are 35 boys in the row, what is A’s position
 from the right?

options.name: 25
26
27
28

questions.solution: Total = 35. A’s position from right = 35 – 10 + 1 = 26.

questions.name: In a code language, CAT = 3120 and DOG = 4157. What will be the code for BAT?
questions.nameText:
In
 a code language, CAT = 3120 and DOG = 4157. What will be the code
 for BAT?

options.name: 2120
3121
2121
2210

questions.solution: Coding rule: Each letter replaced with position in alphabet – 1. C(3-1=2), A(1-1=0), T(20). CAT=3120 (concatenated). Similarly, BAT = 2120.

questions.name: A train of 200m length passes a man standing on a platform in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?
questions.nameText:
A
 train of 200m length passes a man standing on a platform in 10
 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?

options.name: 60
65
72
80

questions.solution: Speed = Distance/Time = 200/10 = 20 m/s = 20×18/5 = 72 km/hr. Correction → Answer is 72 km/hr.

questions.name: If ‘BOOK’ is coded as ‘DSSR’, then how is ‘PEN’ coded?
questions.nameText:
If
 ‘BOOK’ is coded as ‘DSSR’, then how is
 ‘PEN’ coded?

options.name: RGP
RGPQ
RGQ
QGP

questions.solution: Code rule: Each letter shifted +2 in alphabet. B→D, O→S, O→S, K→R. So PEN → R(G)(Q).
